key_insight: A tool-augmented LLM pipeline can turn free-text patient notes into reliable medical calculator outputs by separating clinical variable extraction from deterministic formula execution.
clinical_relevance: This could improve the consistency and trustworthiness of automated clinical scoring and calculation tasks when working with messy real-world notes.
method: Retrieve calculator specs and convert them into executable tools.
Use constrained extraction to map patient notes into calculator-ready inputs.
Run deterministic tool-based calculations instead of relying on the LLM to do the math and formatting.
evidence_signal: On MedCalc-Bench, the method reached 86.73% final-answer accuracy, beating one-shot prompting by 24.0 points and supervised fine-tuning-only baselines by 17.27 points.
watch_item: Remaining errors still cluster around clinical-semantic extraction and strict benchmark-specific output formatting, so deployment would need careful validation.
paper_title: Tool-Augmented Large Language Models for Reliable Medical Calculation from Patient Notes
